scope: Bounded typed response bodies across the Chromium JSON boundary, preserving ordinary control limits and originating closure errors. Functional conformance only; no performance or release claim.

contract.behavior: Typed body replies use borrowed raw envelopes and known-shape decoding; the negotiated decoded cap is validated before copying borrowed bytes. Complete oversized ordinary replies reject only their call. Oversized events or the hard wire cap invalidate the connection. Late cancelled replies do not build result values. Page/context invalidation retains the originating transport failure. Large receive buffers are released after each frame.
contract.limitation: The Chromium JSON frame is still buffered up to the hard wire bound and escaped strings require decoded storage. This is not a constant-memory or streaming CDP decoder. Application attachment frames remain bounded and backpressured.

coverage: Rust tests cover a 9 MiB admitted body with reordered envelope fields, oversized ordinary replies, cancellation midway through a large frame followed by a successful command, fatal oversized events, bounded allocation/release and exact escaped/base64 decoding.

Eight raw real-browser cases include a 9 MiB all-byte binary body and 2 MiB NUL text whose JSON wire representation exceeds 12 MiB, exact data through 32 KiB application frames, negotiated-limit rejection, cancellation, successor reuse and original-error cleanup.
Public TypeScript navigation differentials compare both large bodies byte-for-byte with pinned Playwright and assert exactly one HTTP request per body.

Rebuilding the saved recipe reused cached layers from the pinned Playwright base and Rust 1.98 toolchain, with a newly recorded image identity. Attempt 041 is a separate full verification run; the failed launch and rebuild logs are retained.

The initial driver is retained locally with its separate hash; its preliminary evidence is not a final-binary verification.
